questions.help:
8 Speed limits are a necessity  
   
8.1 The speed limit in a built up area
In a built up area, roads are shared by vehicles and pedestrians and, in the event of a collision, speed is a major factor in the victim's chances of survival. In fact, most pedestrian fatalities occur on urban roads.  
At 30 kilometres per hour, only 5 % of pedestrians involved in a collision die as a result of the accident, while at 50 kilometres per hour, the proportion of deaths is nearly 50%.
(Página 177 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.help:
8 Speed limits are a necessity
 
Speed limits are not capricious. There are numerous factors that determine the implementation of a certain speed limit being imposed, (for example; the designated speed, the acceptable degree of congestion, the demands of existing traffic, etc.) The aim of a set speed limit is to allow vehicles to travel with the maximum guarantee of safety and fluidity.
One of the most important criteria is the designated speed of the road (the maximum safe speed that can be maintained on a section of road under favourable conditions). This means that a road is designated to be used at a certain generic or specific speed limit and traffic is not allowed to do a higher speed than that specified. To do otherwise means that safety will be compromised.
(Página 177 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.help:
9 The negative effects of speed
 
Through the driver’s vision, 90% of the information needed for good driving is received: the condition and configuration of the road, signalling, distances, speeds etc. Hence, the importance of having the largest possible zone of vision when driving. Speed, among other factors, causes a decrease in the useful field of vision, which results in a tunnel vision effect. Therefore, as speed increases the driver’s field of vision is reduced eventually resulting in only objects in the centre of the roadway being clearly visible. The peripheral vision is steadily reduced as speed increases also.
 
(Página 178 del manual 'Learning to drive')

It is prohibited to race on the public highways or in public places. An exception exists when the relevant authorities have authorised an area or location to be used for racing purposes and in accordance with specific controls.
